papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics of Ciona adult brains reveals functional zonalization and insights into neural gland function.
papers.abstract: The ascidian Ciona is a pivotal chordate model for illuminating the evolutionary origins of the vertebrate brain. Here, spatial transcriptomics of the adult Ciona neural complex, combined with image-based computational super-resolution mapping, resolved distinct tissue domains including the cerebral ganglion, neural gland, ciliated funnel, neural gland duct/dorsal strand, and body wall muscle. Within the cerebral ganglion, high-resolution mapping revealed clear molecular zonalization separating the cortex and medulla, alongside regional specialization within the cortex itself. The neural gland
papers.summary: This study applies spatial transcriptomics and computational super-resolution mapping to the adult Ciona neural complex, resolving distinct tissue domains such as the cerebral ganglion, neural gland, and ciliated funnel. It reveals molecular zonalization within the cerebral ganglion, separating cortex and medulla with further regional specialization, and provides new insights into neural gland function. The work offers an evolutionary perspective on the origins of the vertebrate brain.

papers.title: Pan-cancer screening and integrative multi-omics and deep learning reveal the prognostic significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The prognostic relevance of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-colorectal cancer (CRC) shared host-microbe signatures in non-intestinal epithelial malignancies remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic and biological significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe interactome signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA).
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a host-microbe interaction signature previously linked to inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer also has prognostic value in bladder urothelial carcinoma. Using pan-cancer screening combined with multi-omics integration and deep learning, the authors identify and characterize this shared signature in BLCA, suggesting its biological and clinical relevance beyond intestinal cancers.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer, identifying epithelial cell-derived genes that predict immunotherapy response and patient survival. The authors validate ADAM12 as highly expressed in NSCLC tissues and cell lines and demonstrate its functional role through cellular and mouse model experiments. Low-PIS patients show better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, suggesting the signature could guide immunotherapy stratification.

papers.title: Adrenomedullin from spinal cord injury drives heterotopic ossification in skeletal muscle via a neuro-immune-bone axis.
papers.abstract: Neurological heterotopic ossification can rapidly arise in the periarticular muscles following spinal cord injury. However, the specific mechanism of how the injured central nervous system regulates heterotopic bone formation in peripheral tissues remains largely unexplored. Here we first demonstrate through single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analysis that fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs) contribute to heterotopic ossification in injured muscle tissues following spinal cord injury. Mechanistically, we define a neuro-immune-bone axis in which endothelial tip cells with
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to show that fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs) drive heterotopic ossification in muscle after spinal cord injury. The authors identify a neuro-immune-bone axis in which adrenomedullin released after injury signals through endothelial tip cells to promote abnormal bone formation.

papers.title: FABP4 characterizes metabolic-immune interactions and serves as a prognostic biomarker across gynecologic malignancies: a multi-omics integrative analysis.
papers.abstract: Gynecological malignancies-including breast, cervical, ovarian, endometrial cancers and uterine sarcoma-pose a serious threat to women's health owing to their high incidence, aggressiveness and frequent recurrence. Fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) is a key regulator of lipid metabolism and tumor metabolic reprogramming, yet systematic investigations of its role across gynecological malignancies remain scarce. Here, by integrating data from TCGA, GTEx and multiple public repositories, we performed a multi-omics, multi-scale analysis of five gynecological malignancies, encompassing transcrip
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data from TCGA, GTEx, and other public repositories to systematically characterize the role of fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) across five gynecological malignancies. The authors identify FABP4 as a key mediator of metabolic-immune interactions and propose it as a prognostic biomarker across these cancers. The work highlights FABP4's potential as a shared therapeutic target in women's cancers.

papers.title: Vaping reorganizes the pulmonary macrophage landscape into multiple sex-dimorphic microenvironments.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary macrophages are central orchestrators of inflammatory resolution and tissue repair in the lung. Whether vaping-associated macrophage dysregulation is spatially organized, sex-dimorphic, or detectable by bulk transcriptomic approaches remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study examines how vaping alters the landscape of pulmonary macrophages, the immune cells responsible for resolving inflammation and repairing lung tissue. The authors find that vaping reorganizes these macrophages into multiple distinct microenvironments that differ between males and females, and that these changes are not well captured by standard bulk transcriptomic methods. This suggests vaping-induced macrophage dysregulation is spatially organized and sex-specific, requiring more granular approaches to detect.

papers.title: Realistic coupling enables flexible macroscopic traveling waves in the mouse cortex.
papers.abstract: Traveling waves are ubiquitous in neuronal systems across different spatial scales. While microscopic and mesoscopic waves are relatively well studied, the emergence of macroscopic traveling waves remains less understood. Here, by modeling the mouse cortex using spatial transcriptomic and connectivity data, we show that realistic cortical connectivity can generate a significantly higher level of macroscopic traveling waves than artificial local and uniform connectivity across multiple oscillation frequency bands, with the strongest advantage appearing in the theta, alpha, and beta frequency ba
papers.summary: Using spatial transcriptomic and connectivity data to model the mouse cortex, the authors show that realistic cortical connectivity produces far more macroscopic traveling waves than artificial local or uniform connectivity, especially in theta, alpha, and beta bands. This suggests that the brain's actual wiring architecture is key to generating large-scale traveling waves.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study uses multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell data with ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build an ac4C-related gene prognostic signature (acRGBS) for colon adenocarcinoma, identifying four hub genes including TUBA1C. The signature stratifies patients by prognosis and links to immune microenvironment features, with in vitro experiments validating TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: T cell-derived CCL5 drives macrophage immunometabolic remodeling in chronic prostatitis via the CCR5-ERK-PKM2/HIF-1α axis.
papers.abstract: Chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) affects millions of men, yet the immune circuits that sustain sterile prostatic inflammation and pain remain poorly defined. Here we identify a T cell-macrophage metabolic signaling axis that drives chronic prostatitis. Integrated analysis of mouse experimental autoimmune prostatitis, chronically inflamed human prostate tissue, single-cell transcriptomes and spatial profiles revealed a population of glycolytic, HIF-1α-activated inflammatory macrophages enriched in diseased prostate niches. T cell-derived CCL5 was markedly induced and s
papers.summary: This study identifies a T cell-macrophage signaling axis driving chronic prostatitis, where T cell-derived CCL5 activates CCR5 on macrophages, triggering ERK signaling and metabolic reprogramming through PKM2/HIF-1α. The resulting glycolytic, inflammatory macrophage population accumulates in diseased prostate tissue and appears to sustain sterile inflammation and pain. The findings suggest CCR5-ERK-PKM2/HIF-1α as a potential therapeutic target for chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections using only their associated images, without requiring shared molecular features or prior annotations. It enables unified multi-modal spatial datasets and performs comparably to established uni-modal alignment tools across different spatial transcriptomics technologies, tissues, and resolutions.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature related to tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The signature is linked to prognosis and potential therapeutic targets, with TDT reflecting tumor growth kinetics influenced by HPV status and the immune microenvironment.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing, using paired short-read and long-read datasets. The authors systematically compare methods for tasks like isoform detection and alternative splicing analysis, providing guidance on tool performance. The work offers a practical resource for researchers choosing bioinformatics pipelines for long-read single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets of different tensor orders (e.g., third-order drug-response tensors with second-order transcriptomics matrices) by combining group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. It learns interpretable latent factors that capture shared and dataset-specific variation across modalities, addressing a gap in existing integration methods that assume uniform data structures.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: The authors present sPYce, a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without relying on sequence alignment. This addresses a gap where existing single-cell integration methods, designed for gene expression data, perform poorly on chromatin accessibility data. sPYce enables direct comparison of regulatory programs between species to study evolutionary divergence in gene regulation.

papers.title: Decoding cell-cell communication in spatial transcriptomics: mechanistic insights, modeling constraints, and analytical caveats.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is essential for maintaining tissue organization and driving biological progression, yet its inference from transcriptomic data has long been limited by the absence of spatial context. Advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) now enable mechanistically grounded analyses of CCC by preserving the physical organization of cells and their microenvironments. In this review, we examine recent methodological developments in CCC inference from ST data, focusing on how statistical, optimal transport, and deep learning frameworks incorporate spatial information to model lig
papers.summary: This review examines how recent computational methods infer cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data, covering statistical, optimal transport, and deep learning frameworks that leverage spatial context. It highlights mechanistic insights gained, modeling constraints, and analytical caveats that researchers should consider when interpreting such inferences.

papers.title: EGFR-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Small Cell Transformation: Clinicopathological Features, Treatment Landscape, and Biomarker Profiles.
papers.abstract: Transformed small-cell lung cancer (tSCLC) is a clinically important resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. This study characterizes clinical features, treatment outcomes, and biomarker profiles in patients with tSCLC.
papers.summary: This study characterizes transformed small-cell lung cancer (tSCLC), a resistance mechanism that can emerge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer after tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment. It describes the clinicopathological features, treatment outcomes, and biomarker profiles of patients with this transformation, aiming to inform clinical management of this aggressive resistance phenotype.

papers.title: Dietary Polyphenol Acteoside-Related Molecular Signatures in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Multi-Omics Profiling and Functional Validation of IMPDH1.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by substantial metabolic and molecular heterogeneity, but the disease-relevant programs associated with acteoside, a dietary polyphenol, remain poorly understood. We integrated predicted acteoside targets with bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data from ccRCC and combined molecular subtyping with cross-cohort machine-learning analysis. Acteoside-related signatures were preferentially enriched in malignant compartments and increased with tumor grade and stage. Consensus clustering identified two molecular subtypes with distinc
papers.summary: This study integrates predicted acteoside targets with bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data from clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) to define acteoside-related molecular signatures enriched in malignant compartments and associated with tumor grade and stage. Consensus clustering revealed two molecular subtypes, and functional validation identified IMPDH1 as a key player. The work links a dietary polyphenol to ccRCC metabolic heterogeneity and proposes candidate molecular subtypes and targets.

papers.title: Amplification bias in sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics: sources, mechanisms, impacts, and mitigation strategies.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has emerged as a powerful approach for profiling gene expression in spatial tissue context; yet, its quantitative accuracy remains substantially compromised by amplification bias introduced during the complex library preparation process. These biases arise at multiple stages and accumulate throughout the experimental workflow, distorting transcript abundance, reducing detection sensitivity, and ultimately confounding downstream spatial analyses. This review systematically analyzes amplification bias in ST. We examine how input templates, oligonucleotide components
papers.summary: This review systematically analyzes amplification bias in sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics, tracing how biases arise at multiple library preparation stages and accumulate to distort transcript abundance and reduce detection sensitivity. It catalogs the sources and mechanisms of these biases and discusses mitigation strategies to improve quantitative accuracy in spatial analyses.

papers.title: Integrated Genomic and Proteomic Analysis Reveals T-B Lymphocyte Signatures in the MYCN Driven "Immune Desert" of Specific Neuroblastoma Subtypes.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically dissect how MYCN amplification shapes the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in high-risk neuroblastoma, elucidating key mechanisms underlying immune evasion.
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic and proteomic data to dissect how MYCN amplification creates an immunosuppressive 'immune desert' tumor microenvironment in high-risk neuroblastoma. The authors identify distinct T-cell and B-cell lymphocyte signatures that vary across neuroblastoma subtypes, linking MYCN-driven immune evasion to specific immune cell populations. These findings suggest potential immune-related vulnerabilities that could inform subtype-specific therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to analyze ovarian cancer, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor patient outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight the tumor microenvironment, particularly fibroblast heterogeneity and inflammatory signaling, as critical determinants of treatment resistance and adverse prognosis.

papers.title: Stage-specific ROMO1 in rheumatoid arthritis: predictive immune insights into the MIF pathway and HLA-DR/IL2RA axis via integrated GWAS, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial profiling.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence links reactive oxygen species modulator 1 (ROMO1), a key mitochondrial ROS regulator, to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis. However, its exact mechanism remains elusive given the conflicting evidence about its specific function. We used a four-level integrative framework combining multi-omics data and literature‑supported mechanistic inference. At the genetic level, Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed to explore potential causal relationships between ROMO1, IL2RA, HLA-DR, MIF, and RA risk, followed by differential expression analysis and machine learning-based fea
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial data to investigate the role of ROMO1 in rheumatoid arthritis, identifying stage-specific expression patterns and links to the MIF pathway and HLA-DR/IL2RA axis. Using Mendelian randomization and machine learning, the authors propose ROMO1 as a predictive immune marker with potential stage-dependent functions in RA pathogenesis.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing uncovers an immunosuppressive program in PDAC mast cells: tumour-driven activation, proliferation, and association with Treg recruitment.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a highly immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME), which contributes to its resistance to immunotherapy. Although mast cells (MCs) have been implicated in PDAC progression, their functional heterogeneity and candidate signaling models of immune modulation remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize mast cell heterogeneity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), revealing a tumour-driven immunosuppressive program involving mast cell activation and proliferation. The authors link this program to regulatory T cell (Treg) recruitment, suggesting mast cells contribute to the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment that limits immunotherapy response.

papers.title: A skin-kidney neutrophil axis links ultraviolet exposure to renal angiogenesis and tissue remodeling in healthy and lupus kidneys.
papers.abstract: Neutrophils have been implicated in mediating immune crosstalk between injured tissue and distal organs, either promoting local and distal inflammation or mediating tissue repair. Skin injury from ultraviolet (UV) light triggers neutrophil migration to the kidney, which may have implications for nephritis flares in systemic lupus erythematosus. Here, we demonstrate that after skin exposure to UV light, renal neutrophils upregulate proangiogenic transcriptional programs and activate renal endothelial angiogenesis and tissue remodeling processes in healthy kidneys. Ligand-receptor analysis ident
papers.summary: This study shows that ultraviolet (UV) light exposure to the skin triggers neutrophils to migrate to the kidney, where they switch on pro-angiogenic gene programs and promote blood vessel growth and tissue remodeling. This skin-kidney neutrophil axis operates in healthy kidneys and may help explain how UV exposure influences nephritis flares in lupus. The findings reveal an unexpected immune communication route linking skin injury to distant kidney changes.

papers.title: Benchmarking cell type annotation in spatial transcriptomics: resolving cellular hierarchies, biological fidelity, and dynamic cell states.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the quantification of gene expression within its native tissue context, providing unprecedented insight into tissue architecture, cellular ecosystems, and local cell-cell interactions at regional and single-cell resolution. Accurate cell type annotation is a critical prerequisite for interpreting these data and is often the first and most essential step in downstream analysis. Despite rapid advances in computational methods, cell type annotation remains challenging and frequently requires extensive expert-driven manual curation based on marker-gene expression, s
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for cell type annotation in spatial transcriptomics data, evaluating how well they resolve cellular hierarchies, maintain biological fidelity, and capture dynamic cell states. It highlights that accurate annotation remains challenging and often depends on expert manual curation using marker genes, providing guidance on method performance across these dimensions.

papers.title: [Cellular barcoding and next-generation lineage tracing: concepts and applications].
papers.abstract: Lineage tracing is a fundamental technique for dissecting cell fate decisions and development process. With recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and single-cell sequencing technologies, cellular barcoding-based lineage tracing strategies have transitioned from low-throughput labeling methods to high-resolution, multidimensional lineage reconstruction. In this review, we systematically summarize four major barcoding paradigms: viral integration-based random integration barcodes, transposon-based random integration barcodes, recombinase-mediated DNA rearrangement (e.g., Cre-loxP), and C
papers.journal: Sheng li xue bao : [Acta physiologica Sinica]
papers.summary: This review summarizes cellular barcoding strategies for lineage tracing, covering four major paradigms: viral integration-based random barcodes, transposon-based random barcodes, recombinase-mediated DNA rearrangement (e.g., Cre-loxP), and CRISPR-based approaches. It highlights how high-throughput and single-cell sequencing have enabled high-resolution, multidimensional reconstruction of cell fate decisions and developmental processes.

papers.title: Hepatic and Brain Spatial Gene Expression Changes in Intragastric Alcohol Fed APP/PS1 Alzheimer's Disease Mouse Model.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use is increasingly recognized as a significant modifier of Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk and progression. Two key organs, the liver and the brain, are central to understanding the impact of alcohol intake on AD. This is due to the liver being the primary site of alcohol detoxification and a major target of alcohol-induced injury, while the brain harbors the neuropathological hallmarks of AD. Although growing literature now links liver dysfunction to AD pathogenesis, the molecular mechanisms linking peripheral alcohol-induced liver injury to brain pathology remain poorly defined. To ad
papers.summary: This study uses spatial gene expression profiling to examine how chronic alcohol consumption affects both the liver and brain in an APP/PS1 mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. The authors aim to uncover molecular links between alcohol-induced liver injury and AD-related brain pathology, addressing a poorly understood liver-brain axis. The work provides spatially resolved transcriptomic data that could reveal how peripheral organ damage contributes to neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Multimodal Analysis Reveals Aberrant Expression of SUMO2 and Its Significant Association With Key Mechanisms of Metabolic Pathways in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. However, the role of small ubiquitin-like modifier 2 (SUMO2), a core member of the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) family, regarding its expression patterns and metabolism-related functions in HCC remains inadequately understood.
papers.summary: This study uses multimodal analysis to examine SUMO2 expression patterns in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), finding aberrant SUMO2 expression that correlates with key metabolic pathway mechanisms. The findings suggest SUMO2 may play a role in HCC metabolism and could serve as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review surveys 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data, organizing them into three categories: cell-type or single-cell resolution communication networks, microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory modeling, and other analytical frameworks. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone and provides guidance for selecting methods based on the biological question.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: Using a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) in mouse embryonic stem cells, the authors identified epigenetic regulators that control the transition between naive and primed pluripotency states. They found that Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 act antagonistically to orchestrate this pluripotency transition.

papers.title: An hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model exhibiting proximal-distal epithelial features for modeling pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Existing hiPSC-derived lung organoid models are largely restricted to single epithelial lineages and cannot endogenously integrate multiple pulmonary cell types, limiting mechanistic studies and drug screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived multi-lineage lung model that captures both proximal and distal epithelial features, overcoming the single-lineage limitation of prior lung organoid systems. This model enables more physiologically relevant studies of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and could improve drug screening for the disease.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell program—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association signal activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning, the authors link genetic susceptibility to a pathogenic macrophage state in the diseased liver. The work provides a cell-type-specific framework for understanding PSC mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and a boundary wound model reveal temporal decoupling and microenvironmental heterogeneity in radiation-induced fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is a key treatment method for cancer, but high-dose treatment can lead to damage to normal tissues and chronic fibrosis. There is a lack of systematic temporal analysis of the dynamic progression from early damage signals to late extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics combined with a boundary wound model to track how radiation-induced fibrosis develops over time. The authors find that early damage signaling and later extracellular matrix deposition are temporally decoupled, and that the fibrotic microenvironment is heterogeneous across different cell populations. This provides a more systematic temporal map of the transition from acute radiation damage to chronic fibrosis.

papers.title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA.
papers.abstract: Gene expression profiling of single cells using single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sxRNA-seq) enables researchers to characterize cellular heterogeneity and unraveling complex biological processes at unprecedented resolution. However, sxRNA-seq faces challenges due to the presence of ambient RNA, extraneous RNA molecules not originating from the cells of interest. Sample preparation is a major source of ambient RNA, where harsh conditions can lead to cell lysis and the release of intracellular RNA. This inescapable inclusion of ambient RNA can cause erroneous results and hinder dow
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for removing ambient RNA contamination from single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data. Ambient RNA, released from lysed cells during sample preparation, can distort gene expression profiles and lead to false biological conclusions. The study systematically compares available decontamination tools to guide researchers in choosing appropriate approaches.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of MBNL2 associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) improves outcomes in resectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), yet response varies widely and current biomarkers lack precision. Novel correlates of immunotherapy sensitivity tailored to the LUSC tumor microenvironment (TME) are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify MBNL2 as a biomarker associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma. The finding suggests MBNL2 could help stratify patients who are unlikely to benefit from this treatment approach.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures associated with prognosis and immune landscape. The authors identified 630 lactylation-associated genes and used them to characterize the tumor microenvironment and immune infiltration patterns. The findings suggest lactylation-related signatures could serve as prognostic biomarkers and inform immunotherapy strategies in cervical cancer.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of EMCN (endomucin) in lung adenocarcinoma, focusing on its association with vascular-immune crosstalk and its potential as a prognostic biomarker. The authors systematically characterize EMCN expression and its relationship to immune cell infiltration in LUAD, building on prior GWAS links between EMCN mutations and chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression. The findings suggest EMCN could serve as a biomarker reflecting tumor vasculature-immune interactions in LUAD.

papers.title: An integrated SOX4-driven transcriptional and metabolic program governs tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) suppress antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer (OC) and are promising targets for immunotherapy. However, the heterogeneity and regulatory mechanisms of tumor-infiltrating Tregs (TI-Tregs) remain poorly defined. Here, we aim to delineate TI-Treg programs to identify potential therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study characterizes tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells (TI-Tregs) in ovarian cancer and identifies SOX4 as a key transcription factor that coordinates both transcriptional and metabolic programs driving their immunosuppressive function. The findings suggest that targeting SOX4-driven pathways in TI-Tregs could be a therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer.

papers.title: OLR1 as a Key Inflammatory Regulator Associated with Poor Response to Neoadjuvant Immunochemotherapy in Resectable Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Poor pathological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy (nICT) limits long-term survival in resectable lung cancer. How to improve response rates and the regulatory mechanism of tumor inflammatory signaling in nICT efficacy remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study identifies OLR1 (the oxidized LDL receptor 1) as a key inflammatory regulator whose expression is associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in resectable lung cancer. The findings suggest that OLR1-mediated inflammatory signaling may contribute to treatment resistance and could serve as a biomarker or therapeutic target to improve response rates.

papers.title: Association Between Mutation Context-Associated RUNX1 Transcriptional States and Immune-Stromal Heterogeneity in Nonsmall Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in driver mutation backgrounds and tumor microenvironment (TME) phenotypes, yet the transcriptional regulatory states linking genotype context to immune-stromal variation remain incompletely defined. In this study, we integrated mutation, transcriptomic, and clinical data from TCGA-LUAD/LUSC to construct a mutation-expression-matched NSCLC cohort and evaluated RUNX1 as a mutation context-associated transcriptional/regulatory state rather than as a recurrently mutated driver. Driver contexts were assessed using a pr
papers.summary: This study integrates mutation, transcriptomic, and clinical data from TCGA lung adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma cohorts to examine RUNX1 as a transcriptional regulatory state linked to specific driver mutation contexts rather than as a mutated driver gene itself. The authors find that mutation context-associated RUNX1 states correlate with immune-stromal heterogeneity in the tumor microenvironment, suggesting genotype context shapes transcriptional programs influencing immune infiltration.

papers.title: Spatial pharmacology of anti-cancer immunomodulators: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: The field of spatial pharmacology has emerged as a critical framework for understanding the complex interactions between anti-cancer immunomodulators, tumor cells, and the tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution. This review synthesizes the theoretical foundations, historical evolution, clinical applications, diagnostic techniques, therapeutic strategies, and future directions of spatial pharmacology in cancer immunotherapy. By integrating single-cell analysis, signaling dynamics, and multimodal approaches, spatial pharmacology addresses the limitations of traditional "one-size-
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the emerging field of spatial pharmacology, which studies how anti-cancer immunomodulators interact with tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment at single-cell resolution. It covers theoretical foundations, clinical applications, diagnostic techniques, and therapeutic strategies, arguing that spatial approaches overcome the limitations of traditional one-size-fits-all cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification and functional validation of signal regulatory protein gamma as a prognostic biomarker and immune regulator in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) comprises biologically diverse tumors, and durable responses to immune-checkpoint blockade are achieved by only a subset of patients. There remains a need for markers that connect clinical outcome with malignant-cell phenotypes and tissue-level immune organization.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics data to identify signal regulatory protein gamma (SIRPG) as a prognostic biomarker in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, linking its expression to clinical outcomes and immune regulation. Functional validation experiments support SIRPG's role as an immune regulator, suggesting it could help stratify patients for immune-checkpoint blockade therapy.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal SERPINE1 as a Key Link Between Macro_SPP1 Macrophages and Stromal Remodeling in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Macrophage heterogeneity is increasingly recognized as an important feature of the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment, yet the macrophage states linked to poor outcome and the molecules connecting them to stromal remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE183904, spatial transcriptomic data from GSE251950, and TCGA-STAD bulk transcriptomic data to characterize macrophage diversity and identify clinically relevant macrophage-associated genes. papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk TCGA data to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in gastric cancer. The authors identify a macro_SPP1 macrophage population and show that SERPINE1 links these macrophages to stromal remodeling and poor clinical outcomes. The work nominates SERPINE1 as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target in the gastric cancer microenvironment.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis identifies fibroblast IGFBP5 as a key target of anti-TNFα therapy in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Resistance to anti-TNFα therapy (e.g., infliximab) in ulcerative colitis (UC) remains a significant clinical challenge, with the underlying cellular and spatial mechanisms poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to investigate why some ulcerative colitis patients fail to respond to anti-TNFα therapy like infliximab. The authors identify fibroblast-derived IGFBP5 as a key molecular target associated with treatment response, suggesting a potential biomarker or therapeutic avenue for overcoming resistance.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of spatial transcriptomic annotation methods reveals conserved tumor microenvironment programs in NSCLC.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables high-resolution mapping of cellular heterogeneity in tumor microenvironments, but downstream cell-type annotation remains highly method-dependent.
papers.summary: This study systematically benchmarks cell-type annotation methods for spatial transcriptomics data and applies them to non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) tumors. Despite method-dependent differences, the authors identify conserved tumor microenvironment programs across annotation approaches, highlighting robust biological signals that transcend methodological choices.

papers.title: IL1RAP Is Associated With an Inflammation-Immunity-Related State in Skin Cutaneous Melanoma: Integrative Evidence From Pan-Cancer Data and Melanoma Immunotherapy Cohorts.
papers.abstract: The crosstalk between inflammation and immunity plays a central role in tumor progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic response. Interleukin-1 receptor accessory protein (IL1RAP) is a key adaptor in inflammatory signaling, yet its immunological relevance and clinical implications in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of IL1RAP, an inflammatory signaling adaptor, in skin cutaneous melanoma using pan-cancer data and melanoma immunotherapy cohorts. The authors find that IL1RAP is associated with an inflammation-immunity-related state in melanoma, suggesting it may influence tumor progression, immune evasion, and response to immunotherapy.
